claimPolicy: Each claim checked 2026-10-21 by this research worker; verified means supported as documented vendor behavior, never measured or independently audited. Excerpts below map to exact source URLs through source IDs. sources/retrievals.json supplies actual fresh retrieval times, final URLs and original HTML hashes. All feature claims scope to public documentation accompanying the advertised 1.3.11 download, not verified binary behavior.

claims.wording: DeepClean documents macOS 13 Ventura or later on Apple Silicon and Intel.
claims.excerpt: Requires macOS 13 Ventura or later. Apple Silicon and Intel.

claims.wording: Unlimited cleanup is advertised at $39 once for one Mac, without a subscription; currency code and taxes are not explicit in checked text.
claims.excerpt: Unlimited cleanup is a one-time purchase of $39 for one Mac. There is no subscription.
claims.conditions: Personal non-transferable license; major-version updates only; optional future paid major upgrades. Do not call lifetime updates or verified USD/tax-inclusive pricing.

claims.wording: Terms specify a lifetime total of 10 GB moved to Trash per installation for free, but the homepage also says first gigabyte; actual allowance is unresolved.
claims.excerpt: That allowance is a lifetime total per installation, not per scan, and it does not expire.
claims.conflictingExcerpt: Download, scan, and clean your first gigabyte without signing up for anything.

claims.wording: The official install page advertises DeepClean 1.3.11; binary size, signatures, notarization and runtime behavior were not independently checked.
claims.conditions: Existing homepage links https://deepclean.app/DeepClean-1.3.11.dmg; do not fetch installer or bypass download verification.

claims.wording: The website download modal asks for email verification; no account, email submission or download was attempted.
claims.excerpt: Enter your email and we'll send a 6-digit code. Verify it to start the download.
claims.conditions: Do not repeat no email needed: policy later contains conflicting no-email free-scan wording. Website download and in-app scanning are different stages.

claims.wording: DeepClean documents selection before removal, Trash-first movement and Delete History; Caution entries are excluded from bulk selection.
claims.excerpt: Nothing is deleted until you select it, and Caution items are never included in bulk selection.
claims.supportingExcerpt: Removed items go to the Trash rather than being erased, and Delete History records what moved and when.
claims.conditions: Vendor workflow, not safety certification; Trash is not immediate free-space recovery or guaranteed restoration.

claims.wording: The developer page documents Xcode, Node package managers, Cargo, Python caches, Docker, Gradle/Maven and other toolchains.
claims.supportingExcerpt: Global npm cache, Yarn offline mirror, pnpm content-addressable store, and Bun install cache. All four Node.js package managers in one scan.
claims.conditions: Do not adopt typical recovered-GB figures, complete coverage, cache disposability or scan speed as tested facts.

claims.wording: The privacy policy describes local file scanning but networked license activation, updates and optional usage events; blanket no-telemetry/offline claims conflict with it.
claims.excerpt: The only network traffic the app generates goes to our own server: license activation, update checks, optional setup-link confirmation, and a small number of usage events
claims.conflictingExcerpt: No telemetry, no cloud uploads, no accounts.
claims.conditions: Attribute to policy; not a traffic audit. Policy additionally covers user-written support chat and periodic license revalidation with an unspecified offline grace period. Do not imply every network operation is optional.

claims.wording: Full Disk Access is requested for the documented scan; the install guide anticipates a macOS cannot-check warning.
claims.excerpt: DeepClean asks for Full Disk Access when it first opens
claims.conditions: Not a signature inspection. Do not reproduce Gatekeeper bypass instructions or change permissions/settings in research. Python/runtime prerequisites beyond macOS not verified.

claims.wording: DeepClean is licensed software, not source-code ownership; no open-source grant was established.
claims.excerpt: The software itself remains the property of DeepClean; the license gives you the right to use it, not ownership of the code.

claims.wording: The official press kit says high-resolution screenshots are available on request; no app-screenshot republication permission is supplied there.
claims.excerpt: High-resolution screenshots available upon request. Contact us for press-ready assets.
claims.conditions: Do not contact press in this job. Icon download language is not app-UI reuse permission.

claims.wording: Breathing Room, which we build, is a macOS 13+ maintenance preview; the published 0.1.0-preview.1 release discloses Apple Development signing, not Developer ID signing or notarization, Python 3.10+ inventory prerequisites and untested physical Intel runtime.
claims.excerpt: Published preview says Apple Development signed, not Developer ID signed or notarized
claims.evidenceClass: reused same-day capability register; sections Preview, installation and runtime caveats

claims.wording: Breathing Room has documented source implementations for storage views, app/helper CPU/memory grouping, sampled activity history, developer cleanup and exact saved daily approvals while running; this does not prove distributed-binary parity.
claims.excerpt: Source implementation is not proof that every feature works in the distributed installer.
claims.evidenceClass: reused source register; Current capability matrix and Approval exception

claims.wording: Breathing Room advertises a free local desktop core and optional hosted AI Care at $5 USD/month or $50 USD/year; hosted requests require authentication/internet and can send relevant inspection context.
claims.excerpt: Hosted AI assistance requires internet access and authentication; this is not an entirely offline AI product.
claims.conditions: Website account gate differs from public GitHub release download. No tested subscription activation, unlimited-AI entitlement or runtime guarantee.

workflow.title: Review developer storage by rebuild cost, not just folder size
workflow.primaryIntent: Help Mac developers distinguish regenerable caches from environments, Docker data and valuable local artifacts before approving cleanup; use DeepClean's documented ratings as an example, not as proof of disposability.
workflow.distinctAngle: A review worksheet mapping detected category to owning tool, local-only state, backup and rebuild/download cost; not another generic System Data removal checklist.
outline: Conclusion: review recovery cost before selecting a large row
Top visual: DeepClean Developer Tools source once rights cleared
Separate caches from environments, databases and locally authored data
Use Safe/Review/Caution as prompts, not deletion authority
Read the proposed scope and preserve a recovery path
Later visual: labeled Breathing Room Space example and its different investigation model
Choose a one-off scan or investigate recurring growth; unknown competitor monitoring stays unknown
workflow.interactionPass: Handoff a local-only review worksheet: category, owning tool, rebuild method, required downloads, backup status and user decision. No filesystem scan, delete action, upload or invented savings estimate.
workflow.constraints: Do not execute cleanup commands, claim Apple category accounting completeness, repeat typical savings, or prescribe Docker volume/cache deletion. Apple/tool-specific removal guidance needs separate primary-source verification before drafting. Link targets require future site-job validation.

advantagesAndTradeoffs.judgment: A documented one-time, per-Mac license and explicit rated selection/Trash history can fit occasional developer cleanup without a recurring app subscription.
advantagesAndTradeoffs.limits: Major-version update scope; networked activation; conflicting free allowance; no hands-on validation or guarantee of safe removal.

advantagesAndTradeoffs.judgment: Breathing Room, which we build, may fit readers who want source-documented helper grouping, activity context and exact saved daily approvals rather than only a point-in-time storage list.
advantagesAndTradeoffs.limits: Preview, Python requirement, no Developer ID/notarization, hosted authenticated AI and optional recurring AI Care. No claim that DeepClean lacks these features or that Breathing Room is safer/faster.
